basic_info: 41-year-old female with chief complaint of pain at the end of her right middle finger following a car accident a few days ago
present_illness: Pain occurred after a car accident when she hit the ceiling of the car; mechanism of injury: flipping someone the bird and hitting the ceiling. The pain is sharp, stabbing, and constant, rated 7 or 8 out of 10. There is tenderness at the tip of the finger, swelling, and it appears slightly bent. The patient can move the finger but experiences significant pain during movement. No numbness or tingling reported. The patient was informed of a suspected fracture but has not yet received X-ray results. No specific advice on pain management or immobilization has been provided yet.
past_history: No previous injuries or conditions affecting the hand or fingers. This is the first time something like this has happened.
physical_exam: Tenderness at the tip of the right middle finger, swelling, and slight deformity (bent appearance). Full range of motion is limited due to pain.
aux_exam: Imaging studies: X-ray of the right middle finger was mentioned but results are not yet available.
